annotation.material_differences: Response C adds a more definitive operational stance: it would close the ticket again unless the customer can show a new error, and it says to keep trying a few more times. That is a different follow-up/confirmation mechanism and a stronger assumption about the fix than A/B, which simply ask the customer to try again and reopen/submit a new ticket if it still fails, with no explicit re-closure or extra retry condition. C also introduces a stronger expectation-management claim that the original fix can be assumed to have failed if it still does not work after multiple tries.
annotation.equivalence_rationale: A and B are materially aligned: both communicate that the issue should be fixed, ask the customer to retry, and route them to a new ticket or issue report if it still fails, without promising additional follow-up. C differs in a way that could affect all three criteria, especially follow-up and expectation management, because it adds repeated retry instructions, a decision to close the ticket again, and an assumption about diagnosing the fix based on continued failure. Those are operational commitments not preserved in A/B.
